title: Partial Identification of Fine-Time VAR Impulse Responses from Two Unaligned Sampling Clocks
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 (typed) BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR — D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field (target=field); not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The field-level framing is not delivered because the general sharp set is characterized only through existential real-algebraic projection: the note provides neither an algorithm that outputs its components and endpoints nor recheckable certificates beyond hand-derived fixtures.

The finite-sample result establishes conservative containment conditional on externally supplied dependence envelopes, but gives no size or informativeness guarantee and the projected set may be practically vacuous.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived the two-clock Gaussian transition fiber, its affine dimension bound, query-specific impulse certificates, an open family with joint-only identification, and conditional finite-sample set coverage. Both D0.5 correctness panels passed, but the cold novelty review graded the delivered work incremental against the fixed field floor. A field-level result would require the exact elimination backend, independently checkable certificates, and complexity theorem that this topic left open; no Lean formalization was started.
tldr: The field-level object is sharp partial identification of fine-time Gaussian VAR impulse responses from two unaligned clocks. In the singular regime, the compatible transition fiber lies in \(ZB_2=B_3=B_2Z\), has residual dimension at most \((d-\operatorname{rank}B_2)^2\), and is cut out by quadratic power and diagonal-noise constraints; each scalar impulse image is therefore an exact bounded semialgebraic union of intervals and points. Linear-query multipliers, singular countermodel fixtures, strict two-clock improvement over the rate-two fiber, and identification of all horizons \(h\ge2\) support the kernel. Conservative finite-sample projection is uniformly valid only conditional on fixed externally known dependence envelopes. Causal impulses are the application, and the graph is only a support restriction. No claim is made for polynomial time, full graph recovery, generic rank-adaptive inference, or a production exact backend.
gap: Published subsampling work gives qualitative graph equivalence or generic whole-parameter retrieval, while published SVAR set methods emphasize isolated branches, extrema, or asymptotic projection. These results do not characterize the singular two-clock Gaussian transition fiber and its full scalar images.
fill: The project derives the two-sided affine kernel and \((d-r)^2\) bound, proves the quadratic fiber and scalar semialgebraic geometry, supplies representation-invariant query certificates and compatible countermodels, and adds strict clock comparison and conservative externally calibrated coverage.
